QF.id: Role of RTAs in Mutual Fund Transactions_17

question.text: The custodian of a mutual fund must be:

answer.text: A subsidiary of the AMC managing the fund
Appointed by SEBI directly for each scheme
The same entity as the RTA servicing the fund
Independent of the sponsor of the mutual fund

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI requires the custodian to be a SEBI-registered entity that is independent of the sponsor of the mutual fund. This independence prevents conflicts of interest because the custodian holds the fund's securities. The RTA workbook notes that the custodian is the only constituent of a mutual fund that is not directly appointed by the AMC — the trustees appoint the custodian. The Trap: SEBI does not appoint the custodian for each scheme; SEBI sets the framework and registers eligible custodians. The custodian is not appointed by the AMC either — that role belongs to the trustees. Sponsor-affiliation is the disqualifier. Note: The custodian holds all the securities bought by the fund. Independence from the sponsor and trustee-level appointment together ensure that investor assets are safeguarded even if the AMC or sponsor faces difficulties.
